reviewNote: Nut AI installs unsigned onto the reader's own phone, and photo scans run on publik API by default from a bounded key the phone mints (the reader's own key also works). The guide says both before the first command.

steps.title: Copy Nut AI to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d nut-ai/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/nut-ai.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: A nut-ai folder appears

steps.title: Open the nut-ai folder
steps.command: cd nut-ai
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the nut-ai folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.command:
(
if ! git config --get remote.origin.url 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's#^git@github\.com:#https://github.com/#; s#\.git$##' | grep -qxF "https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/nut-ai"; then
  echo "~/nut-ai already exists and is not a clean copy of this app's source. Move or rename that folder, then press Try again."
  exit 1
fi
if git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
  echo "~/nut-ai already exists and is not a clean copy of this app's source. Move or rename that folder, then press Try again."
  exit 1
fi
git checkout dace89160b86de38165a952100860f47f1010177
)
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

expect.prompt: In the terminal, below a git checkout command, does git report 'HEAD is now at dace891'?

hints: The 'detached HEAD' paragraph above that line is normal here, not an error.
'reference is not a tree' means the clone was interrupted — delete ~/nut-ai and clone again.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.body: Vulnerability warnings at the end are expected here — don't run npm audit fix.
steps.command: npm install
steps.verifierLabel: The command finishes without an error

steps.title: Build the nutrition database
steps.body: It downloads the USDA tables itself first (about 10 MB). Re-running it is always safe.
steps.command: npm run data:build
steps.verifierLabel: It ends with 'Built …/nutrition.db' and foods: 7928

expect.prompt: Does the terminal show a line beginning 'Built' with a nutrition.db path, and a foods count near 7928?

hints: A download failure prints the exact USDA URL and why — paste it into a browser to check, then rerun.
If USDA retired a release, override it: FDC_FOUNDATION_RELEASE=<date> npm run data:build.

steps.title: Install Xcode
steps.body: Large — start now. Not compatible? Get an older Xcode: developer.apple.com/download/all
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode opens without asking to finish setup

hints: The App Store button reads Open once the download is finished.
First launch asks to install additional components — let that finish before going on.

steps.title: Install CocoaPods
steps.body: The iPhone project generator needs CocoaPods. Does nothing if you already have it.
steps.command:
brew list cocoapods >/dev/null 2>&1 || brew install cocoapods
pod --version
steps.verifierLabel: pod prints a version number

steps.title: Generate the iPhone project
steps.command:
cd apps/mobile
npm run prebuild
steps.verifierLabel: It ends with the use-release-scheme message

steps.title: Open the project in Xcode
steps.command: open ios/NutAI.xcworkspace
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode opens with the NutAI project

hints: Open the .xcworkspace, not the .xcodeproj — the project on its own has no pods.
No ios folder? The step before this one did not finish.

steps.title: Sign the app with your Apple ID
steps.body: Signing & Capabilities: set a unique Bundle Identifier (com.yourname.nutai), then pick your Team.
steps.verifierLabel: Signing & Capabilities shows no red error

expect.prompt: In Xcode's Signing & Capabilities tab, is a Team selected and the red 'requires a development team' error gone?

hints: 'Failed Registering Bundle Identifier' or 'cannot be registered to your development team'? The shipped com.nutai.app is already taken. Change the Bundle Identifier field to a unique string (com.yourname.nutai), then let Xcode retry. A free Apple ID works. 'No profiles for com.nutai.app were found' goes away once it registers.
No team in the list? Add your Apple ID first: Xcode → Settings → Accounts.
Leave 'Automatically manage signing' ticked — a free Apple ID cannot do it any other way.

An error naming HealthKit means a free Apple ID can't get that entitlement (Apple's restriction). Build without it: SKIP_HEALTHKIT=1 npm run prebuild, then reopen the workspace and set your unique Bundle Identifier again (prebuild regenerates ios/ and resets it to com.nutai.app). A paid developer account restores Health sync.

steps.title: Plug in your iPhone
steps.body: Unlock it, tap Trust, then pick it from the device menu.
steps.verifierLabel: Your iPhone is selected as the run destination

steps.title: Press Run
steps.body: The ▶ button. The first build takes a few minutes.
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode finishes with Build Succeeded

steps.title: Trust yourself on the iPhone
steps.body: On the phone: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → your Apple ID → Trust.
steps.verifierLabel: Your Apple ID shows as trusted

steps.title: Open Nut AI on your iPhone
steps.body: Scans run on publik API; link the phone when asked. Free signatures last 7 days — Run renews.
steps.verifierLabel: Nut AI opens on your phone

steps.title: Install Java 17
steps.body: The Android build needs Java 17 or newer. Installs Temurin 17 if Java is missing or older.
steps.command:
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] && "$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -version 2>&1 | grep -Eq 'version "(1[7-9]|[2-9][0-9])'; then
  echo "$JAVA_HOME" > ~/.nut-ai-java-home
else
  /usr/libexec/java_home -v 17+ >/dev/null 2>&1 || brew install --cask temurin@17
  /usr/libexec/java_home -v 17+ > ~/.nut-ai-java-home
fi
read -r JAVA_HOME < ~/.nut-ai-java-home && export JAVA_HOME
"$JAVA_HOME/bin/java" -version || { echo 'Java 17 or newer is still missing. Install Temurin 17 from adoptium.net, then run this step again.'; false; }
steps.verifierLabel: java -version prints 17 or newer

expect.prompt: Does the last java -version output in the terminal show version 17 or newer (openjdk version "17..." or higher), not 1.8 or 11?

hints: A JDK installed a moment ago only appears in a terminal opened afterwards.
brew missing? Download Temurin 17 from adoptium.net and run the installer, then come back.

steps.verifierLabel: An android folder appears inside apps/mobile

steps.title: Download the Android build tools
steps.body: The first run downloads Gradle and the Android NDK. Later runs take about a minute.
steps.command:
[ -f ~/.nut-ai-java-home ] && read -r JAVA_HOME < ~/.nut-ai-java-home && export JAVA_HOME
[ -n "$ANDROID_HOME$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT" ] || [ ! -d "$HOME/Library/Android/sdk" ] || export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
"${ANDROID_HOME:-$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/platform-tools/adb" shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abilist 2>/dev/null | tr ', \r' '\n\n\n' | grep -m 1 -x -E 'armeabi-v7a|arm64-v8a|x86|x86_64' > ~/.nut-ai-abi
read -r ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures < ~/.nut-ai-abi || ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a
export ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures
./gradlew help
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Build the libraries' C++ code
steps.body: Compiles the libraries' C++ code for your phone's processor only. Keep the phone plugged in.
steps.command:
[ -f ~/.nut-ai-java-home ] && read -r JAVA_HOME < ~/.nut-ai-java-home && export JAVA_HOME
[ -n "$ANDROID_HOME$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT" ] || [ ! -d "$HOME/Library/Android/sdk" ] || export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
"${ANDROID_HOME:-$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/platform-tools/adb" shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abilist 2>/dev/null | tr ', \r' '\n\n\n' | grep -m 1 -x -E 'armeabi-v7a|arm64-v8a|x86|x86_64' > ~/.nut-ai-abi
read -r ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures < ~/.nut-ai-abi || ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a
export ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures
./gradlew externalNativeBuildRelease -x :app:externalNativeBuildRelease
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.title: Build the libraries and app C++ code
steps.body: Compiles the libraries' Kotlin and Java code and the app's own C++ code.
steps.command:
[ -f ~/.nut-ai-java-home ] && read -r JAVA_HOME < ~/.nut-ai-java-home && export JAVA_HOME
[ -n "$ANDROID_HOME$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT" ] || [ ! -d "$HOME/Library/Android/sdk" ] || export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
"${ANDROID_HOME:-$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT}/platform-tools/adb" shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abilist 2>/dev/null | tr ', \r' '\n\n\n' | grep -m 1 -x -E 'armeabi-v7a|arm64-v8a|x86|x86_64' > ~/.nut-ai-abi
read -r ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures < ~/.nut-ai-abi || ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a
export ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures
./gradlew assembleRelease :app:externalNativeBuildRelease -x :app:assembleRelease
steps.verifierLabel: Gradle prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL

steps.body: Builds the app, installs it on your phone and opens it.

[ -f ~/.nut-ai-java-home ] && read -r JAVA_HOME < ~/.nut-ai-java-home && export JAVA_HOME

unsupported.headline: A Windows PC cannot build an iPhone app
unsupported.reason: Apple only allows iPhone apps to be built and signed on macOS using Xcode, which Apple does not release for Windows. This is Apple's restriction, not a missing feature in Nut AI or Iris — no setup, emulator, or virtual machine makes it work reliably.
alternatives: Borrow a Mac for about thirty minutes — the signature it installs lasts 7 days and can be renewed on any Mac.
Use an Android phone instead, which builds fine from Windows.
